scope: Numbers 9–10, all 59 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 9–10. All 59 exact original records are hashed, including eight source annotations across 9:3, 9:10, 9:21, 10:9, 10:25, 10:34 and 10:36. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Move the full date to the opening so the reader locates the Passover account before the census; retain speaker, recipient and Sinai setting.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they came out from the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.after: In the first month of the second year after the Israelites left Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they came out from the land of Egypt, saying,

verses.rationale: Retain Passover and appointed time as recurring anchors; convey the jussive as an instruction.
verses.before: “Let the Israelites keep the Passover at its appointed time.
verses.after: “The Israelites are to keep the Passover at its appointed time.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let the Israelites keep the Passover at its appointed time.

verses.rationale: Retain day fourteen, appointed time and both all-statute/all-regulation clauses; twilight matches Exodus 12, with the disputed between-the-evenings idiom noted.
verses.before: On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you will keep it at its appointed time. According to all its statutes and all its ordinances you will keep it.”
verses.after: Keep it at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month, its appointed time. Follow all its statutes and all its regulations.”
verses.tsw_comparator: On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you shall keep it at its appointed time. According to all its statutes and all its ordinances you shall keep it.”

verses.rationale: Render speaking plus purpose as instructed, preserving the command’s transmission and named participants.
verses.before: So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover.
verses.after: Moses instructed the Israelites to keep the Passover.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated exact date and location, with a separate command-fulfillment sentence instead of compressing the repetition.
verses.before: They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the Israelites did.
verses.after: They kept the Passover in the wilderness of Sinai, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. The Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the Israelites did.

verses.rationale: Keep the men as a specific group, corpse-related ritual impurity, inability rather than refusal, and both same-day references; no invented moral fault.
verses.before: But there were some men who were unclean through contact with a dead person, so that they could not keep the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that day,
verses.after: But some men were unclean because of a dead person and could not keep the Passover that day. That same day they came before Moses and Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: But there were some men who were unclean through contact with a dead person, so that they could not keep the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that day,

verses.rationale: Resolve him as Moses and preserve the men’s question about exclusion from the communal offering; appointed time remains explicit.
verses.before: and those men said to him, “We are unclean through contact with a dead person. Why should we be kept from presenting the LORD’s offering at its appointed time among the Israelites?”
verses.after: They said to Moses, “We are unclean because of a dead person. Why should we be kept from bringing the LORD’s offering at its appointed time with the rest of Israel?”
verses.tsw_comparator: and those men said to him, “We are unclean through contact with a dead person. Why should we be kept from presenting the LORD’s offering at its appointed time among the Israelites?”

verses.rationale: Render stand as wait in context and preserve Moses’ need to hear rather than presenting an immediate personal ruling.
verses.before: Moses said to them, “Wait, and I will hear what the LORD commands concerning you.”
verses.after: Moses answered, “Wait here while I hear what the LORD commands concerning you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to them, “Wait, and I will hear what the LORD commands concerning you.”

verses.rationale: Retain the distinct speech boundary before the answer to the men’s question.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Express the distributive anyone and future generations inclusively, retaining both exceptions and distant as written despite its extraordinary dot; permission continues with the alternate date.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: If someone among you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead person, or is on a distant journey, that person may still keep the Passover to the LORD.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: ‘Anyone among you or your descendants who is unclean because of a dead person, or away on a distant journey, may still keep the Passover for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: If anyone among you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead person, or is on a distant journey, that person may still keep the Passover to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep second month distinct from the original first-month date, retain twilight and both meal accompaniments.
verses.before: They will keep it in the second month, on the fourteenth day at twilight. They will eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
verses.after: They are to keep it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month, eating it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall keep it in the second month, on the fourteenth day at twilight. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

verses.rationale: Retain both prohibitions and all applicable Passover statutes; it still refers to the sacrifice rather than to an abstract festival.
verses.before: They will leave none of it until morning and break none of its bones. According to every statute of the Passover they will keep it.
verses.after: They must leave none of it until morning and must not break any of its bones. They are to follow every statute for the Passover.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall leave none of it until morning and break none of its bones. According to every statute of the Passover they shall keep it.

verses.rationale: Preserve both conditions and the severe cut-off sanction, with its reason and bearing sin; generic legal person is inclusive, while the sanction’s unspecified mechanism remains open.
verses.before: But anyone who is clean and is not on a journey yet fails to keep the Passover—that person will be cut off from the people, because the LORD’s offering was not presented at its appointed time. That person will bear their sin.
verses.after: But anyone who is clean and not away on a journey, yet fails to keep the Passover, will be cut off from their people. They did not bring the LORD’s offering at its appointed time; they must bear their sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: But anyone who is clean and is not on a journey yet fails to keep the Passover—that person shall be cut off from the people, because the LORD’s offering was not presented at its appointed time. That person shall bear their sin.

verses.rationale: Retain resident status, conditional participation, both legal terms and one shared rule; do not add broader civic claims or silently waive Exodus 12’s conditions.
verses.before: If a resident alien lives among you and keeps the Passover to the LORD, according to the statute of the Passover and according to its ordinance, so will that person do. You will have one statute for both the resident alien and the native of the land.”
verses.after: If a resident foreigner lives among you and keeps the Passover for the LORD, that person must follow its statutes and regulations. You are to have one rule for the resident foreigner and the native-born alike.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: If a resident alien lives among you and keeps the Passover to the LORD, according to the statute of the Passover and according to its ordinance, so shall that person do. You shall have one statute for both the resident alien and the native of the land.”

verses.rationale: Keep tabernacle/tent-of-testimony identification and appearance rather than assert ordinary combustion; preserve evening-to-morning duration.
verses.before: On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony; and from evening until morning it was over the tabernacle like the appearance of fire.
verses.after: On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered it—the tent of the testimony. From evening until morning, something like fire appeared over the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the Tent of the Testimony; and from evening until morning it was over the tabernacle like the appearance of fire.

verses.rationale: Preserve the continuing pattern without importing the words by day from other witnesses; clarify the nocturnal appearance from verse 15.
verses.before: So it was continually: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.
verses.after: It was always this way: the cloud covered the tabernacle, and at night it had the appearance of fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: So it was continually: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.

verses.rationale: Make the matched movement and stopping conditions audible, retaining the repeated named people and then sequence.
verses.before: Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, afterward the Israelites set out; and in the place where the cloud settled, there the Israelites camped.
verses.after: Whenever the cloud rose from above the tent, the Israelites would then set out. Wherever the cloud settled, the Israelites would make camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, afterward the Israelites set out; and in the place where the cloud settled, there the Israelites camped.

verses.rationale: Retain both occurrences of the mouth-of-the-LORD command idiom and the complete duration condition.
verses.before: At the command of the LORD the Israelites set out, and at the command of the LORD they camped. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.
verses.after: At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they made camp. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they stayed in camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the command of the LORD the Israelites set out, and at the command of the LORD they camped. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.

verses.rationale: Preserve many days, keeping charge and the explicit negative; connect the charge wording with the preceding Levite responsibilities.
verses.before: Even when the cloud remained over the tabernacle many days, the Israelites kept the charge of the LORD and did not set out.
verses.after: Even when the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the LORD’s charge and did not set out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even when the cloud remained over the tabernacle many days, the Israelites kept the charge of the LORD and did not set out.

verses.rationale: Render days of number as a few days in contrast with many; keep the repeated command refrain instead of reducing it to a summary.
verses.before: Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle only a few days; at the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out.
verses.after: Sometimes the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for only a few days. At the LORD’s command they stayed in camp, and at the LORD’s command they set out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle only a few days; at the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out.

verses.rationale: Retain the overnight case and read day/night as times of departure, noting the alternative duration reading; bind both source accent and punctuation annotations exactly.
verses.before: Sometimes the cloud remained from evening until morning, and when the cloud lifted in the morning they set out. Whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted, they set out.
verses.after: Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening to morning. If it rose in the morning, they set out. By day or by night, whenever it rose, they set out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sometimes the cloud remained from evening until morning, and when the cloud lifted in the morning they set out. Whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted, they set out.

verses.rationale: Preserve two days/month/year sequence, interpreting days as year in this extended-duration idiom with alternative noted; keep both the negative and positive movement clauses.
verses.before: Whether two days, a month, or a longer time, as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, resting upon it, the Israelites remained in camp and did not set out; but when it lifted, they set out.
verses.after: Whether the cloud stayed over the tabernacle for two days, a month or a year, the Israelites remained in camp and did not set out. When it rose, they set out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whether two days, a month, or a longer time, as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, resting upon it, the Israelites remained in camp and did not set out; but when it lifted, they set out.

verses.rationale: Preserve all four divine-name occurrences, both command refrains, keeping charge and Moses as mediator; do not omit the concluding repetition.
verses.before: At the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out. They kept the charge of the LORD according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
verses.after: At the LORD’s command they made camp, and at the LORD’s command they set out. They kept the LORD’s charge, following the LORD’s command given through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the command of the LORD they camped, and at the command of the LORD they set out. They kept the charge of the LORD according to the command of the LORD through Moses.

verses.rationale: Retain a distinct divine speech opening for the silver trumpet regulations.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retain two, silver and hammered workmanship, with both assembly and departure functions clear; do not identify them as ram’s horns.
verses.before: “Make two silver trumpets for yourself; make them of hammered work. Use them for summoning the congregation and for setting the camps in motion.
verses.after: “Make two trumpets of hammered silver for yourself. Use them to call the community together and to signal the camps to move.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Make two silver trumpets for yourself; make them of hammered work. Use them for summoning the congregation and for setting the camps in motion.

verses.rationale: Resolve plural them against the single trumpet of verse 4; preserve the whole community, Moses and exact assembly location without prematurely naming the blowers.
verses.before: When both are blown, the whole congregation will gather to you at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: When both trumpets are blown, the whole community is to gather before you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: When both are blown, the whole congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keep one trumpet distinct from two, retain the thousands designation as a social/military grouping and clarify that the leaders are summoned.
verses.before: But if only one is blown, the leaders, the heads of Israel’s thousands, will gather to you.
verses.after: When just one is blown, the leaders—the heads of Israel’s thousands—are to gather before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if only one is blown, the leaders, the heads of Israel’s thousands, shall gather to you.

verses.rationale: Keep the specific teruah signal and east-side camps; do not invent the signal’s pitch, length or number of notes.
verses.before: When you sound a signal blast, the camps on the east will set out.
verses.after: When you sound the alarm signal, the camps on the east are to set out.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you sound a signal blast, the camps on the east shall set out.

verses.rationale: Preserve second/south and the repeated departure signal; do not add west/north signals absent from the pinned Hebrew.
verses.before: When you sound a second signal blast, the camps on the south will set out. A signal blast will be sounded for their setting out.
verses.after: At the second alarm signal, the camps on the south are to set out. The alarm signal is to be sounded for their departures.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you sound a second signal blast, the camps on the south shall set out. A signal blast shall be sounded for their setting out.

verses.rationale: Retain the deliberate distinction between an assembly blast and teruah; avoid assigning an unattested modern musical pattern.
verses.before: But when the assembly is gathered, you will blow the trumpets without sounding the signal blast.
verses.after: To gather the assembly, blow the trumpets, but do not sound the alarm signal.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when the assembly is gathered, you shall blow the trumpets without sounding the signal blast.

verses.rationale: Keep priestly sons as the authorized blowers and enduring instruction, with its generational scope.
verses.before: The sons of Aaron, the priests, will blow the trumpets. This will be a perpetual statute for you throughout your generations.
verses.after: Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to blow the trumpets. This is a lasting statute for you through all your generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be a perpetual statute for you throughout your generations.

verses.rationale: Keep war in their land, oppressive adversary, trumpet signal, remembered-before-God language and rescue; do not convert this into a general endorsement of war.
verses.before: When you go to war in your land against an adversary who oppresses you, you will sound the signal with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and be saved from your enemies.
verses.after: When you go to war in your own land against an enemy who oppresses you, sound the alarm on the trumpets. You will be remembered before the LORD your God and rescued from your enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you go to war in your land against an adversary who oppresses you, you shall sound the signal with the trumpets, and you shall be remembered before the LORD your God and be saved from your enemies.

verses.rationale: Retain the three occasions, two offering categories and memorial before God, linked to remembered in verse 9; beginnings of months preserves the calendar expression without imposing a modern date.
verses.before: Also on your days of rejoicing, your appointed festivals, and the beginnings of your months, you will blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your sacrifices of well-being. They will be for you as a remembrance before your God. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.after: On your days of rejoicing, at your appointed festivals and at the beginnings of your months, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace-offering sacrifices. They will be a reminder on your behalf before your God. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Also on your days of rejoicing, your appointed festivals, and the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your sacrifices of well-being. They shall be for you as a remembrance before your God. I am the LORD your God.”

verses.rationale: Retain all three date components and the tabernacle-of-testimony term marking departure.
verses.before: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.after: In the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, the cloud rose from above the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle of the testimony.

verses.rationale: Render journeys as staged movement while preserving both wilderness names; do not imply this was their only intermediate stop.
verses.before: Then the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai by stages, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
verses.after: The Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai, traveling by stages, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai by stages, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.

verses.rationale: Keep the first-departure frame within the Sinai account and the divine command mediated by Moses, not a claim Israel had never traveled before.
verses.before: They set out for the first time according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
verses.after: This was their first departure at the LORD’s command given through Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out for the first time according to the command of the LORD through Moses.

verses.rationale: Resolve his division as Judah’s while retaining banner, first position, divisions and the named commander and father.
verses.before: The standard of the camp of the Judahites set out first by their divisions, and over its division was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
verses.after: The camp of Judah set out first under its banner, arranged in its divisions. Nahshon son of Amminadab led Judah’s division.
verses.tsw_comparator: The standard of the camp of the Judahites set out first by their divisions, and over its division was Nahshon son of Amminadab.

verses.rationale: Retain Issachar’s unit and Nethanel/Zuar identification, using active led for the over idiom.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Issachar was Nethanel son of Zuar.
verses.after: Nethanel son of Zuar led the division of the tribe of Issachar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Issachar was Nethanel son of Zuar.

verses.rationale: Preserve the next tribal unit and both personal names in the same readable command pattern.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Zebulun was Eliab son of Helon.
verses.after: Eliab son of Helon led the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Zebulun was Eliab son of Helon.

verses.rationale: Preserve dismantling and the two carrying clans in this position, without adding an unstated actor for taking it down.
verses.before: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried the tabernacle, set out.
verses.after: The tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites set out carrying it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and Merarites, who carried the tabernacle, set out.

verses.rationale: Retain the next banner group, divisions and Elizur/Shedeur; clarify whose division is commanded.
verses.before: Then the standard of the camp of Reuben set out by their divisions, and over its division was Elizur son of Shedeur.
verses.after: The camp of Reuben set out under its banner, arranged in its divisions. Elizur son of Shedeur led Reuben’s division.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the standard of the camp of Reuben set out by their divisions, and over its division was Elizur son of Shedeur.

verses.rationale: Preserve Simeon’s position and both names, joining the repeated command pattern without omitting the verse.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Simeon was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
verses.after: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai led the division of the tribe of Simeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Simeon was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

verses.rationale: Keep Gad’s unit and Deuel as written here and in 7:42, without harmonizing Reuel in 2:14.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Gad was Eliasaph son of Deuel.
verses.after: Eliasaph son of Deuel led the division of the tribe of Gad.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Gad was Eliasaph son of Deuel.

verses.rationale: Render carrying the sanctuary as its holy things in the context of chapters 4 and 7; distinguish the Kohathites’ arrival from the unnamed plural who set up the tent, using passive rather than a false same-subject reading.
verses.before: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The others would set up the tabernacle before they arrived.
verses.after: The Kohathites set out carrying the holy things. By the time they arrived, the tabernacle would already be set up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The others would set up the tabernacle before they arrived.

verses.rationale: Preserve Ephraim’s group after Kohath and all command identifiers.
verses.before: Then the standard of the camp of the Ephraimites set out by their divisions, and over its division was Elishama son of Ammihud.
verses.after: The camp of Ephraim set out under its banner, arranged in its divisions. Elishama son of Ammihud led Ephraim’s division.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the standard of the camp of the Ephraimites set out by their divisions, and over its division was Elishama son of Ammihud.

verses.rationale: Preserve Manasseh’s subordinate unit, named leader and father without compressing the list.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Manasseh was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
verses.after: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur led the division of the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Manasseh was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

verses.rationale: Keep Benjamin and Abidan/Gideoni in sequence, with active English for the command relationship.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.
verses.after: Abidan son of Gideoni led the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.

verses.rationale: Render the gathering-up role as rear guard in the march context; retain all camps, division structure, leader and exact source punctuation annotation.
verses.before: Then the standard of the camp of the Danites set out as the rear guard for all the camps, by their divisions, and over its division was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
verses.after: The camp of Dan set out under its banner, arranged in its divisions, as the rear guard for all the camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai led Dan’s division.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the standard of the camp of the Danites set out as the rear guard for all the camps, by their divisions, and over its division was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

verses.rationale: Retain Asher, Pagiel and the established Ochran spelling from earlier Numbers batches.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Asher was Pagiel son of Ochran.
verses.after: Pagiel son of Ochran led the division of the tribe of Asher.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Asher was Pagiel son of Ochran.

verses.rationale: Preserve the last named tribal unit and its leader/father, without omitting the repeated structural wording.
verses.before: Over the division of the tribe of Naphtali was Ahira son of Enan.
verses.after: Ahira son of Enan led the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the division of the tribe of Naphtali was Ahira son of Enan.

verses.rationale: Make the closing journeys statement read as the summary of the ordered divisions while retaining the setting-out clause.
verses.before: This was the order of setting out for the Israelites by their divisions whenever they set out.
verses.after: This was the Israelites’ marching order by divisions when they set out.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was the order of setting out for the Israelites by their divisions whenever they set out.

verses.rationale: Retain Hobab/Reuel/Midian and use a broader marriage-kin term with father-in-law and attachment uncertainties noted; preserve quoted promise and repeated good language leading to verse 32.
verses.before: Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will do good to you, for the LORD has spoken good concerning Israel.”
verses.after: Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ relative by marriage, “We are setting out for the place the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will do good to you, because the LORD has promised good for Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will do good to you, for the LORD has spoken good concerning Israel.”

verses.rationale: Identify the reply’s speaker, retain refusal and both land and kin destinations; do not assert he ultimately left.
verses.before: But he said to him, “I will not go; rather, I will go to my own land and my own kindred.”
verses.after: Hobab answered, “I will not go with you. I am going back to my own land and my own people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said to him, “I will not go; rather, I will go to my own land and my own kindred.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the plea, wilderness-camping knowledge and eyes image rather than replacing it with a generic guide alone.
verses.before: Moses said, “Please do not leave us, for you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be eyes for us.
verses.after: Moses said, “Please do not leave us. You know where we can camp in the wilderness. You can be our eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “Please do not leave us, for you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be eyes for us.

verses.rationale: Retain the clear existing wording after source comparison: the conditional invitation and repeated good relationship are accurate and readable; no acceptance by Hobab is supplied.
verses.before: If you come with us, whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do for you.”
verses.after: If you come with us, whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If you come with us, whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do for you.”

verses.rationale: Retain both three-day references and the ark’s forward position and searching purpose; do not turn journey duration into a three-day gap or harmonize the earlier order of holy things.
verses.before: So they set out from the mountain of the LORD on a journey of three days, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them for those three days to seek out a resting place for them.
verses.after: They traveled from the mountain of the LORD for three days. The ark of the LORD’s covenant went ahead of them on that three-day journey to seek out a resting place for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they set out from the mountain of the LORD on a journey of three days, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them for those three days to seek out a resting place for them.

verses.rationale: Retain daytime covering and departure condition; exact raw source includes the inverted-nun annotation following this verse.
verses.before: The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
verses.after: The LORD’s cloud was over them by day whenever they set out from camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.

verses.rationale: Keep habitual invocation, divine enemies and haters, and the direct appeal; preserve poetic parallelism and its force inside the verse paragraph.
verses.before: Whenever the ark set out, Moses said: “Rise up, O LORD, and let your enemies be scattered; let people who hate you flee before you.”
verses.after: Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say: “Rise, LORD! Let your enemies scatter; let those who hate you flee before you!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whenever the ark set out, Moses said: “Rise up, O LORD, and let your enemies be scattered; let those who hate you flee before you.”

verses.rationale: Retain the paired resting invocation, return and both large-number terms without reducing them to an exact census total; to is supplied for the compressed relation, noted alongside source boundary marks.
verses.before: And whenever it came to rest, he said: “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel.”
verses.after: When the ark came to rest, he would say: “Return, LORD, to Israel’s myriads of thousands!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And whenever it came to rest, he said: “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel.”
